results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Audited all 51 aligned prose/list units, p01–p51, in order; the independent summaries match the controlling ideas, including the arithmetic restriction, conditional individual/team comparison, operational questions, and understanding hand-off. The introductory callout is mapped to null as evidence attached to p01, rather than counted as an extra paragraph.

Audited p01–p51 and both flagged outline entries: the callout is an intentional multi-point summary, and p22’s task-dependence evidence and warning about unlike measures serve one job, interpreting what those results establish. The examples in p13/p26/p31, coordination and table framing in p35, practical moves in p44, and questions in p46 likewise elaborate a single controlling purpose rather than unrelated claims.

Every unit traces to the declared claims: the introduction and p05–p18 establish S1; p19–p23 establish S2; p24–p32 establish S3; p33–p36 join S2/S3; p37–p43 establish S4; p44–p46 apply S5; and p47–p51 synthesize their declared claims. The callout and annotated reference apparatus also support that argument, with no unconnected substantive unit.

Audited all 47 declared evidence items, all five actual tables (including the limits table), all five figures/captions, the six declared quotation items, and the annotated references: each has an interpretation in its text, caption, table cells, or adjacent prose. Examples include METR’s perception/result distinction, the separate outcome labels before Figure 2, the lifecycle chart’s non-measured status, the queue mechanism, the conditional framing around the team table, and preparation versus checking around the Monday table; remaining summary-wording friction is recorded under flow_is_followable rather than treated as missing explanation.

Audited all 38 within-container transitions, all 12 incoming section/conclusion transitions, and the concluding hand-off: the actual prose carries the declared information and relationship throughout p01–p51. Representative links include “Task dependence is another part of this scatter,” the chain-of-stages elaboration after ownership cost, “The shared review stage also decides what quality reaches the codebase,” the practical application of organizational foundations, and understanding as “One of those constraints.”

Both independent flow readers reconstruct the complete model → limits → task evidence → ownership → bottleneck → team → quality → organization → action/question → synthesis route and explain why each of the 11 body sections belongs where it is. This matches the declared problem_solution pattern and the prerequisite_order, small_to_large, comparison, and assertion_evidence_reasoning sequences; all reported local rereading points are recorded separately below.

results.draft_locus: It Amplifies Speed (in Both Directions), Figure 2 caption after ¶4 (p22)
results.quote: The same AI runs from roughly minus nineteen percent (experienced developers on familiar code) to plus thirty-nine percent (juniors), depending on the user and the task's fit to the frontier.
results.finding: Both readers had to return to the earlier explanation because the caption presents one AI on a numerical speed range immediately after the prose says the studies use different measures and cannot share such a scale. The contract requires this caption verbatim while requiring that incompatible interpretation to be prevented; the protected caption needs an author decision, not another unqualified pass for the surrounding explanation.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-2.txt, Issue 1 independently identifies the same Figure 2 sentence and the same apparent common speed scale; flow-reader-1.txt, item 1 reports the matching reread.

results.draft_locus: Why Your Team Didn't Get Faster (Even Though You Did), Individual row in the table after ¶3 (p35)
results.quote: Reliably positive, and *felt* strongly. This part of the accelerator story is basically true.
results.finding: Flow reader 2, Issue 2 had to reread the explicit measured-positive-case lead-in because the table’s general labels and unqualified positive row seemed to contradict METR. Flow reader 1 explicitly found the conditional comparison understandable, so this is an uncorroborated local scope problem; whether more scoping can resolve it without changing the protected table remains unclear.

results.draft_locus: What to Do on Monday, standards row in the table after ¶1 (p44)
results.quote: Evals, tests, review, a clear definition of "good" — in front of the generator, not after. They decide the sign.
results.finding: Flow reader 2, Issue 3 had to return to the preparation-versus-checking explanation because “not after” appeared to exclude applying checks to generated work afterward. Flow reader 1 explicitly found the lead-in sufficient, so this is an uncorroborated local contradiction in the summary wording; whether additional framing can resolve it without editing the protected table remains unclear.

Audited first uses and paragraph openings across p01–p51 against the carried audience of engineers and technical leaders: amplification/sign, task frontier, ownership, bottleneck/throughput, coordination, quality checks, and organizational foundations are explained or concretized before their later applications. Cross-links supply their relevant meaning locally, and both flow readers’ remaining concerns concern contradictory summaries, not an independently reported undefined term.

The callout and p01–p04 open with the concrete purchasing-and-distribution scenario, explain its appeal, state a disputable alternative and practical consequence, and announce the route and evidence. This is none of the enumerated placeholder, restated-question, dictionary, dawn-of-man, or book-report patterns.

Audited p47–p51: the conclusion answers the established what/which-stage questions, adds their combined delivery criterion, and hands off understanding already introduced as ownership work in p25 and p44. It neither delays the thesis/evidence nor adds an unrelated subtopic, emotional appeal, or thesis-only ending; no enumerated weak conclusion pattern applies.

Across p47–p50, input quality and the location of the constraint are combined into a decision about which work deserves investment, and the final criterion is whether gains reach people relying on the system instead of becoming waiting work or maintenance. That combines the task, ownership, standards, and throughput strands and supplies the declared reason to care.

The conclusion’s opening “Accelerator”/pedal comparison directly returns to the purchasing story in p01–p02, then replaces how hard to press with “amplify what?” and “amplify which part?”. Its final recommendation develops precisely the callback declared in /conclusion/callback.

The introduction-only reader predicted the metaphor and its limits, contrasting task studies, perceived versus measured speed, downstream ownership and bottlenecks, the individual/team gap, standards and organizational foundations, and practical actions/questions, along with comparison tables and the forceful conversational tone. All five roadmap promises are fulfilled in the body’s actual order; the reader did not need body-only details to identify the route.

The AC-1 cold reader explains dependence on people, tasks, goals, checks, and organizational context; describes contrasting slowdown/perception and adjacent-task correctness evidence; and explicitly rejects a fixed formula or common speed scale. The answer also identifies both required limits: new capabilities and variable gains, including adverse results.

The AC-2 cold reader explains the growing review queue as a local generation gain feeding unchanged downstream capacity, identifies integration and other shared stages, and connects extra changes with coordination and ownership work that can worsen delivery. The answer proposes examining the actual constraint and does not assume AI must improve review, satisfying the expected local-versus-system and ownership explanation.

The AC-3 cold reader proposes real-work comparisons that separate time, completed tasks, correctness, and perception; follows outcomes through queues, delivery stability, integration, coordination, and full ownership costs; and improves quality criteria, context, review capacity, and the actual constraint before expanding generation. The answer distinguishes preparing checks from applying them afterward and treats numerical effects and budgets as questions for local evidence.
